recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的細胞內充滿粗大、深紫黑色、大小不一的嗜鹼性顆粒，顆粒覆蓋並遮蔽細胞核，細胞周邊顆粒排列最明顯，旁邊的帶狀嗜中性球顆粒細小，對照可認出這是嗜鹼性前驅細胞（basophilic myelocyte）。
features: Medium-to-large cell (arrow) packed with coarse, dark purple-black basophilic granules of variable size
Granules overlie and partly obscure a round nucleus; granules are most discrete at the cell periphery
Nucleus round, non-segmented, consistent with an immature (myelocyte-stage) basophil
Adjacent band/metamyelocyte neutrophils with fine granules for comparison
Background of scattered free granules from ruptured cells and marrow precursors
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear at high power shows a granulocytic precursor (arrow) with a round, non-segmented nucleus densely overlaid by coarse, dark purple-black granules of variable size. Adjacent neutrophilic band forms and metamyelocytes contain only fine granules. Scattered free granules are present in the background, likely from disrupted cells. Findings are consistent with a basophilic precursor (basophilic myelocyte).

ddx.vs: Mast cells are larger and round-to-spindle with a central nucleus and uniform, tightly packed granules that fill the cytoplasm evenly, whereas basophil granules are larger, fewer, and more variable, overlying a lobulating nucleus in mature forms.
Promyelocyte granules are reddish-purple azurophilic granules with a perinuclear Golgi hof, not black-purple granules overlying the nucleus.

ddx.dx: Eosinophilic precursor with immature basophilic-staining granules
ddx.vs: Early eosinophil granules may stain dark but are uniform, round, and accompanied by orange-red mature granules, unlike the irregular black-purple granules here.
